components.css: .ds-board{width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;text-align:left;font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:13px;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;color:var(--color-ink);background:var(--color-ground)}.ds-board thead tr{border-bottom:1px solid var(--color-rule-strong)}.ds-board thead th{padding:8px;font-family:var(--font-sans);font-size:11px;font-weight:400;letter-spacing:.025em;color:var(--color-ink-3)}.ds-board tbody tr{height:36px;border-bottom:1px solid var(--color-rule)}.ds-board tbody tr:hover{background:var(--color-wash)}.ds-board td,.ds-board tbody th{padding:4px 8px}.ds-board tbody th{font-family:var(--font-sans);font-weight:300}.ds-board .rk,.ds-board .c{color:var(--color-ink-3)}.ds-board .r{text-align:right}.ds-rate{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:flex-end;gap:12px}.ds-track{display:block;flex:1;min-width:40px;height:6px;border-radius:9999px;background:var(--color-wash)}.ds-bar{display:block;height:6px;border-radius:9999px;background:var(--color-delayed);transition:width .5s}.ds-val{width:56px;text-align:right;color:var(--color-delayed)}@keyframes ds-lamp{from{background-color:rgba(232,165,75,.2)}to{background-color:rgba(232,165,75,0)}}.ds-lamp>td,.ds-lamp>th{animation:ds-lamp 1.2s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) forwards}@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-lamp>td,.ds-lamp>th{animation:none}}

narrative.overview:
Every ranking is a departure board. Airlines, airports, routes and months are rows in fixed tabular columns on a near-black ground, and the delay rate is the lit amber column. The system rejects the category default of a grey card grid of identical chart tiles: blocks are separated by hairline rules, not boxes, and a single page reads top to bottom as one continuous board.

The world is dark and quiet so the data can glow. Ink is warm off-white stepped down in three levels; colour is spent only on encoding data (the dusk palette), never on decoration. A serif (Instrument Serif) gives page titles and headline figures a printed, editorial voice; Geist carries the interface; Geist Mono with tabular figures carries board rows so digits line up like split-flap characters. Density is high but calm: 36px rows, 11-13px UI text, and generous 40px gutters between the main column and the side column.

There is one moment of material: the Predict panel is the only glass surface, because scoring a flight is the one place the visitor acts rather than reads. Motion is reserved for the signature move: when a board re-sorts or refilters, rows glide to their new rank and changed rows hold an amber lamp, then fade.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black ground (#010101), warm ink stepped by three levels, hairline rules instead of cards.
Dusk palette as data encoding: amber delayed, blue on time, red cancelled, violet NAS, green weather.
Serif for titles and headline figures, Geist for UI, Geist Mono tabular figures for data.
Departure-board tables with an inline delay-rate bar and a lamp on re-rank.
One glass surface, on Predict only.
Every data block has loading, error-with-retry and empty states.

rules.name: The Lit Column Rule
rules.body: Amber means delayed or delay rate. If a value is not about delay, it is not amber; a non-delay share uses the ink tone of RateCell.

rules.name: The Paired Encoding Rule
rules.body: Delayed versus on time is always amber versus blue, in every chart, gauge, factor bar and matrix.

rules.name: The Colour Is Data Rule
rules.body: Saturated colour appears only to encode a data category. Chrome, buttons and headings stay in ink.

rules.name: The Mono Means Measured Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono is for figures, dates, codes and IDs. Names (airlines, airports, features) inside a mono board switch back to Geist.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Labels and column heads are sentence case at 11-12px in ink-2 or ink-3. There are no uppercase eyebrow labels above titles.

rules.name: The One Glass Rule
rules.body: Glass (the `liquid-glass` treatment) exists only on the Predict panel and its submit button. Every other surface sits flat on the ground.

rules.name: The No-Card Rule
rules.body: Blocks are divided by hairline rules, not boxed in cards with shadows or fills.

dos: Do show rankings and breakdowns as departure boards: fixed tabular columns, Geist Mono tabular figures, 36px rows, hairline dividers.
Do use Departure Amber (#e8a54b) only for delayed flights or delay rates, and pair it with Dusk Blue (#7c9bd1) for on time.
Do separate blocks with hairline rules (rgba(255,255,255,0.08)) and a serif section title.
Do set page titles, section titles and headline figures in Instrument Serif at weight 400.
Do keep Geist Mono for figures, dates, codes and IDs, and switch names back to Geist.
Do wrap every API-backed block in QueryState so it has loading, error-with-Retry and empty states.
Do honour `prefers-reduced-motion`: no glide, no lamp, no rise, near-zero transitions, poster image instead of video.
Do use the 2px amber focus ring (3px offset) for every interactive element.
donts: Don't build card grids of identical chart tiles or put content in shadowed cards.
Don't use amber for anything that is not about delay (decoration, headings, generic highlights, buttons).
Don't use the glass treatment anywhere except the Predict panel and its submit button.
Don't set prose, names or headings in Geist Mono.
Don't add uppercase eyebrow labels above titles; labels are sentence case.
Don't add drop shadows; the only shadow is the glass inset highlight.
Don't show any number the API does not provide.
